issues.description: The template implementation of simulate_ghz_state in tensor_networks.py is missing the shots parameter in its function signature, yet the problem statement and the solution expect simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits, shots). The template's simulate_ghz_state definition only accepts num_qubits and then references shots in the docstring and asserts (shots > 0), which is undefined. This is a structural mismatch that will prevent students from running or testing the GHZ simulation and misleads them about the required function signature.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the template function signature to include the shots parameter to match the problem specification and the solution: def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]:. Update the docstring/ asserts accordingly so that shots is a defined parameter (e.g., assert shots > 0). This keeps the pedagogical intent intact while removing a blocking structural error.

issues.description: The Tensor-Networks GHZ simulation function is specified in the problem statement (and implemented in the solution) to accept both num_qubits and shots (simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits, shots)). The template implementation, however, defines simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits) (no shots parameter) while its docstring and body refer to a shots variable (e.g., asserting shots > 0). This creates a misleading API mismatch: students reading the problem will expect to implement/ call simulate_ghz_state with a shots argument, but the template's function signature omits that parameter. This inconsistency will cause confusion and likely runtime/name errors when students try to follow the problem or match the solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template function signature match the problem statement and solution by adding the shots parameter. Change the template declaration from def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int) -> dict[str, int]: to def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]: and ensure the docstring and body consistently reference the shots parameter.
